Homework: GPT-2 vs GPT-3 – Understanding LLM
Training
Overview
In this assignment, you will read the GPT-2 and GPT-3 papers, summarize the differences between
the two models, describe the general training process of a large language model (LLM), and then
find an open-source implementation to train on your own dataset. The goal is to understand both
the conceptual evolution from GPT-2 to GPT-3 and the practical challenges of training a language
model.
Required reading:
•Radford et al., “Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners” (GPT-2, 2019).
https://cdn.openai.com/better-language-models/language_models_are_unsupervised_multitask_
learners.pdf
•Brown et al., “Language Models are Few-Shot Learners” (GPT-3, 2020).
https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165
Part 1: Paper Review – GPT-2 vs GPT-3 & LLM Training Process
(40 points)
1. Read both the GPT-2 and GPT-3 papers.
2.Summarize the differences between GPT-2 and GPT-3 (about half a page). Decide for
yourself which aspects are most important to discuss based on what you read in the two papers.
3.Describe the general training process of an LLM (about half a page). Cover the stages
you think are essential, in your own words.
Part 2: Find Open-Source Code, Train on Your Own Data, and
Report Problems (60 points)
Task 2A: Find an Open-Source Implementation
1. Search for and choose an open-source GPT-2 or GPT-3-style implementation. You decide which
one to use. State clearly in your report:
◦The repository name, URL, and author.
◦The license.
◦Why you chose it (readability, popularity, documentation, etc.).
2. Briefly describe the structure of the repository: where the model is defined, where training is
launched from, and how the dataset is loaded.
1

Task 2B: Train on Your Own Dataset
1. Choose or assemble a text dataset of at least ˜1M tokens. It can be anything: books, song lyrics,
Wikipedia articles in a specific topic, code, dialogue, your own writing, etc. State which dataset
you used and the total token count after tokenization.
2. Adapt the data-preparation pipeline of the repository you chose so it works on your dataset
(split into train/val, tokenize, save in the format the repo expects).
3. Train a small model. Use whatever configuration fits on the hardware you have access to (free
Google Colab GPU is fine). Suggested starting point: 4–6 layers, embedding dimension 256–384,
context length 128–256, 2000–5000 iterations.
4. Generate text from your trained model with at least 3 prompts and at least 2 sampling
configurations (e.g., greedy and top- p= 0.9 with temperature 0 .8). Include the generations in
your report.
Task 2C: Identify and Report Problems
1. Report the following measurements from your training run:
◦Final training loss and validation loss.
◦Validation perplexity.
◦A plot of training and validation loss vs. iteration number.
2.Identify at least 3 problems you encountered during this assignment. For each problem,
write 2–4 sentences covering: what the problem was, how you noticed it, and what you tried
(or could try) to fix it. Problems can come from any stage of the work: setting up the repo,
preparing the data, the training run itself, or the quality of the generations.
3. Write a short discussion (about half a page) reflecting on:
◦Whether your model captures the style of your training data — give one concrete example
from the generations.
◦What you would change if you had 10 ×more compute.
◦One thing about LLM training that surprised you.
2

Grading Rubric
Criteria Points
Part 1: Paper Review (40 pts)
•Both papers read and properly cited 4
•GPT-2 vs GPT-3 differences — clarity, accuracy, depth 18
•LLM training process — clarity, accuracy, depth 18
Part 2: Code, Training, and Problem Report (60 pts)
•Open-source repo found, cited, and structure described (Task 2A) 10
•Dataset prepared correctly and adapted to the chosen repo (Task 2B) 10
•Model trained with logged training run 10
•Generations on ≥3 prompts with ≥2 sampling strategies 5
•Loss/perplexity reported and loss-curve plot (Task 2C) 10
•At least 3 problems identified, described, and analyzed 10
•Discussion of style, scaling, and surprises 5
Total 100
Submission Checklist
□Your data-preparation script
□Your training config / command
□Training logs and loss-curve plot
□Saved generations
□report.pdf (2–3 pages)
Compute Requirements
A free Google Colab GPU (T4) is sufficient. Expected training time: 30–90 minutes depending on
configuration.
